text:
emma-cs: FYI ACME reported sustained 429s and P95 latency >2s during their 09:00 UTC morning burst. They say autoscaling didn't add nodes. Ticket #12345.

sahil-support: taking it, can you paste the dedicated pool id and the exact time window? any recent config changes on their end?

emma-cs: pool_id: ded-az1-acme, spike window 2025-07-03 08:58:00 -> 09:06:00 UTC. No changes reported from customer. Baseline qps ~150, spike to ~900 for ~7m.

maya-oncall: looked at metrics — GPU utilization hits ~98%, queue length spikes, instance count stayed at 5 the whole time. Autoscaler logs show scale attempts but capped by max_instances=5. Looks like pool was undersized for that peak. :thinking_face:

sahil-support: can you paste the pool config?

maya-oncall: config snapshot:
```
pool_id: ded-az1-acme
min_instances: 2
max_instances: 5
target_utilization: 0.75
scale_cooldown_secs: 120
burst_capacity: disabled
```

maya-oncall: note the max_instances=5 — at 900 qps 5 instances overloaded (avg ~180 qps/instance) and target_utilization prevents further scaling. Also scale_cooldown is 120s which slowed ramp.

julie-eng-runtime: tagging in — runtime behavior looks expected given that config. Two quick options: bump max_instances and enable burst_capacity, or increase min_instances to match expected peak baseline. We should also check if our autoscaler rejected launches due to infra quota (rare).

sahil-support: customer wants a fast mitigation without surprises to billing. alex-sales — any guidance on handling potential overage while we expand capacity?

alex-sales: suggest enabling temporary burst_capacity and set an agreement note that any auto-scale above committed will be billed at overage rate. Offer to open a one-off uplift for today if needed. Customer prefers minimal ops friction.

emma-cs: customer agreed to temporary burst. Can ops enable?

ops-bot: @sahil-support request accepted. Provision change queued.

deploy-bot: change applied to pool ded-az1-acme at 2025-07-03T09:12:30Z by ops. New config:
```
min_instances: 4
max_instances: 20
burst_capacity: enabled
scale_cooldown_secs: 30
```

maya-oncall: monitoring after change: within 3m P95 dropped to 180-320ms and 429s cleared. GPU utilization distributed across more instances. :thumbsup:

sahil-support: want to capture repro steps so eng-runtime can add guidance to docs. Repro script used (internal):
```
# quick spike repro (unsafe for prod)
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
    -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
    -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-dedicated-1\",\"input\":\"load test\"}' &
done
wait
```

julie-eng-runtime: filing a follow-up to add autoscaler doc notes: recommend customers set max_instances based on observed peak qps and a safety factor (we'll suggest formula). Also we should expose a recommended 'burst headroom' toggle in console. Adding action item ENG-PI-789.

maya-oncall: one more note — noisy-neighbor not applicable (dedicated pool). This was pure mis-sizing + cooldown. Marking incident root cause: pool configuration insufficient for peak + conservative cooldown.

emma-cs: customer update posted — they saw immediate improvement and will monitor 24h. They asked for our recommended target numbers; rough calc I shared: if baseline 150 qps and peak 900 qps, set max_instances >= ceil(peak / expected_qps_per_instance). For A100-40 we recommend 250-300 qps per instance for simple gen workloads, so max_instances ~4 for baseline but 900/275 ~4? (this looks off) — hold on, we will compute precisely and send.

sahil-support: haha yes please do exact calc before sending. :slightly_smiling_face:

alex-sales: we'll also follow up on contract to add burst buffer for predictable spikes.

emma-cs: closing the thread once customer confirms stable for 24h. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
